subject: BrightCart — elevated 5xx/timeouts on model 'zenith' (customer impact & postmortem)
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@brightcart.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>; ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: devops@brightcart.com
Date: Fri, 1 Mar 2029 09:12:22 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 504s hitting model-zenith on our production endpoints

Hi Neha / Ben —

We started seeing a spike of 504 / timeout errors from the BrightCart production integration beginning ~03:00 UTC this morning. Error rates peaked around 03:30–03:50 UTC and affected a subset of long-context requests (user session histories ~12k tokens).

Examples (request IDs): 5f8a9c2d, 5f8a9e1b, 5f8aa4f0. The failures are consistent across both our EU and US routes to model 'zenith' and are causing checkout flow slowdowns for ~2% of sessions. Our logs show the client-side retries occur 3–4 times before falling back to cached responses.

Can you confirm if this is an isolated degradation on your side or if we should keep routing to a fallback model? We can enable a temporary abort/shorter timeout on our side if that would help.

Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Integrations — BrightCart


From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Intermittent 504s hitting model-zenith on our production endpoints

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the quick heads up and the example request IDs. We're opening a Sev-2 investigation now. My initial ask: can you share a single raw request+response (redact PII) and the approximate average token length for the failing requests? That will help us reproduce locally.

Immediate actions we are taking:
- Triage with backend/model serving (Ben + Marcus on this) to see whether a specific model variant is producing the 5xxs.
- If we confirm a model-level regression, we'll route traffic to the compatible fallback variant and apply a temporary batch-size cap.
- I'll update you with an ETA for a mitigation step within 15–20 minutes.

Appreciate the patience — we'll follow up with specifics once Ben has had a chance to pull runtime logs.

Regards,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Intermittent 504s hitting model-zenith on our production endpoints

On Fri, Mar 1, 2029 at 09:25 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Immediate actions we are taking:
> - Triage with backend/model serving (Ben + Marcus on this) to see whether a specific model variant is producing the 5xxs.

Status update: we confirmed elevated 5xx/timeouts coming from the quantized variant "zenith-v2-quant" running on a subset of hosts serving long-context traffic. Root cause appears to be KV-cache fragmentation leading to sporadic memory pressure and internal RPC timeouts when sequences exceed ~8k tokens under heavy batching.

Mitigation applied (09:35 UTC):
- Temporarily rolled traffic for long-context routes to "zenith-v1" (non-quant) for BrightCart's account to avoid the quant-specific failure path.
- Reduced max batch size from 64 -> 24 for affected hosts and enabled stricter per-request mem caps.
- Restarted the two hosts showing repeated OOM traces.

Observed impact: error rate dropped from ~4.2% -> 0.3% for your sample traffic within ~4 minutes of mitigation. We've attached a short log excerpt showing the repeated RPC timeouts and the restart markers (ops_rpm_log_snippet.txt).

Work in progress: Marcus is collecting more telemetry to validate there are no lingering slow paths. We'll keep this route on the fallback variant until we deliver a safe config/patch.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: BrightCart — zenith 5xxs post-incident summary and remediation plan

Sanjay —

Thank you again for the quick escalation and patience while we validated the fix. Below is the post-incident summary and proposed remediation timeline. We've attached a draft postmortem (postmortem-brightcart-zenith.docx) and shared the same in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDEF_postmortems/brightcart-zenith

Incident summary (timeline)
- 2029-03-01 03:00 UTC — BrightCart reports spike in 504/timeouts for long-context requests.
- 2029-03-01 03:12 UTC — Initial customer report received by Redwood integrations.
- 2029-03-01 03:25 UTC — Internal triage identifies elevated RPC timeouts in "zenith-v2-quant".
- 2029-03-01 03:35 UTC — Mitigation: traffic routed to "zenith-v1" for long-context routes; batch size capped; two problematic hosts restarted.
- 2029-03-01 03:40 UTC — Error rate reduced to baseline (~0.3%).

Root cause
- A quantization-specific memory fragmentation bug in the "zenith-v2-quant" runtime path when serving sequences >8k tokens under large batch sizes. This caused intermittent RPC failures and internal timeouts.

Immediate remediation (completed)
- Routed BrightCart long-context traffic away from the affected variant.
- Decreased batch sizes and added per-request memory caps on susceptible hosts.

Planned longer-term fixes (timeline)
- Short (2 weeks): fix memory fragmentation in quant runtime and release a patched "zenith-v2-quant" build (target 2029-03-15).
- Medium (4–6 weeks): add a conservative circuit-breaker and auto-fallback rule in the routing layer specifically for quant variants when median sequence length exceeds 6k.
- Monitoring: add additional per-variant mem-pressure alerts and request-context size telemetry dashboards (ETA 2029-03-08).

Customer impact and credits
- We estimate BrightCart experienced an elevated error window of ~40 minutes affecting approximately 2% of sessions. Per our SLA, this should be considered for a pro-rated credit; I'll follow up with finance/renewals and our account team (Jordan) to propose a credit (expected preliminary offer: 5% of monthly usage for March) by 2029-03-04.

Attachments
- postmortem-brightcart-zenith.docx (draft) — contains full logs, timelines, and technical root-cause analysis.
- ops_rpm_log_snippet.txt — included in earlier message with relevant RPC timeout traces.

Next steps for BrightCart
- Jordan will coordinate the formal credit and contract/renewal implications.
- We'll schedule a technical sync (30–45 min) to walk through the root cause and confirm the release plan for the patched quant variant. Proposal: 2029-03-12 16:00 US/PST — please confirm availability.

If you want any changes to the postmortem doc before we publish it internally and to the account team, let us know. We're treating this with high priority and will keep you updated on the patch release.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
